propositions: The byte-equivalence test oracle invokes both production _convert and a copied _legacy_convert subprocess for all 884 corpus units, with the copied oracle reading mutable production constants instead of pinned expected outputs, making the oracle unable to detect format mutations in production.

Pandoc 3.6.1 exists as platform-specific binaries with different SHA-256 values across macOS arm64 (94ebf1efbce3561379e8f25de3efe5aeabee64dc36dd8e8b9e96cf05b4195c52) and Linux x86_64 (4715627586c5d9c732e8f5a6b6bb9e27c4216a76a7729e043b24374dedf8a1f0); the fixture schema must store and validate the complete platform fingerprint map, not a single hash.

Replacing the copied _legacy_convert subprocess with immutable golden outputs reduces 884 redundant Pandoc invocations per test run while preserving all 884 real production _convert calls, eliminating coupling and improving oracle independence.

The fixture must record generating Pandoc version, platform/architecture context, and platform-keyed binary fingerprints; validation must reject version drift, unknown platforms, and fingerprint mismatches with diagnostics before any conversion attempt.
